test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Given below is a statement followed by two possible underlying assumptions I and II. Read the information carefully and select the correct option.

**Statement:**

Extracts of plant C have been found useful in treating an earlier fatal disease. Although plant C, once imported, can be grown on any moist soil, most pharma companies in country Y are still choosing synthetic substitutes over using natural extracts.

Which of the following can be assumed by the given statement?

I. Unlike the case in all other countries, in Country Y, production of this synthetic substitute is substantially cheaper than growing Plant C.

II. The effect of a synthetic substitute is not drastically different from the plant extract.

options.text: Both I and II can be assumed
Neither I nor II can be assumed

solution:
**Statement:****
Extracts of plant C have been found useful in treating an earlier fatal disease. Although plant C, once imported, can be grown on any moist soil, most pharma companies in country Y are still choosing synthetic substitutes over using natural extracts.

**Assumptions:**

I. Unlike the case in all other countries, in Country Y, production of this synthetic substitute is substantially cheaper than growing Plant C → The statement tells us about the usefulness and preference of the extracts but no part of it considers the prices being cheaper or expensive in any way so the assumption here does not support the given statement.

II. The effect of a synthetic substitute is not drastically different from the plant extract → From the part 'most pharma companies in country Y are still choosing synthetic substitutes over using natural extracts' we can assume that the companies are very much satisfied with the performance of synthetic substitutes, so it is used over plant extract and it is not drastically different therefore the assumption is true.

So, **only II can be assumed.**

Hence the correct answer is " Only II can be assumed ".**
